chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: The 1958 Seven Ages of Jazz and travelling with Billie Holiday
summary: Her occasional appearances in 1958; Billie Holiday sat beside her on the small plane and seemed bitter.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, anyway, okay so you were playing then after '56?
Oh, maybe once a year on a

special occasion or something.
Alright, but as we said, in '58 on July the 27th you did that Jazz Festival.
Yes.
And then two months later, in September you went out to that presentation called "The Seven Ages of Jazz" that Leonard Feather promoted out in Connecticut.
Yeah, yeah. These were just those rare occasions. I didn't consider myself in the business.
It's good you did that because that has given us two performances of your's on record.

Yes, I guess among the musicians you know, they know you're around and this is not the business end of it. This is the artistic end of it. And Leonard called me because he was making a presentation and of course I was supposed be all the singers, Mildred Bailey, Ella Fitzgerald, and Billie Holiday, and I was representing the female singers, until I guess the news got back that I was doing "Lover Man" and Billie got out of her sick bed and came and did her own "Lover Man".

She made two. Two of the songs she sang came out on record. I forget what the other one was but it was a terrific performance.

I really don't know. She was terrific that night. She wasn't well but you know, the sparks just flew all over the place. And this was the only time that I and Billie Holiday had ever been in the same place at the same time. That is close enough to have a conversation. We worked on the stoop but we weren't associates. See, I didn't do much hanging around. When I got off of work I'd go home. I didn't run into too many people in the after-hours clubs.
So do you remember having a conversation with her?
Oh yes, we flew up in a small plane. We sat right next to each other. We talked all the way up. Then we shared a dressing room and we were just like buddy-buddy, you know.
Do you remember what you talked about?
Oh, she was sort of rambling about some of the things, you know, that she had been
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

through and all that. So far as I'm concerned Billie was quite bitter about something. I don't know what but she wasn't a very happy person. So all I did was listen. I was pretty much overwhelmed pretty much by even being in the same room with Billie Holiday, you know. She's great. But she did her numbers and she was terrific. I think it was shortly after that she passed, I'm not sure how soon after that.
I think it was in the early part of '59. So that would be six months or nine months after. Okay, so you don't remember anything more specific about that encounter with her?

No, not really because after it was all over it was a one night stand she went home and I went back. I understood from a friend of mine who was considered to be pretty close to Billie, I don't know whether she was a distant relative or what, but Billie used to live here in the Bronx in this particular area I understand. And there was a theater up here on Boston Road that had live entertainment and I think Billie appeared there. They had live entertainment there for quite a spell, probably before I moved up here.
